title: Standby Spells pre-build the mitigation path so emergency engineering effort can go to the root cause
content:
A.1.10.5.2.1 explains the problem Standby Spells solve. Sky Protocol's circuit breakers are MOM contracts, which "must first be triggered through a Spell, after which they bypass the GSM Pause Delay and can immediately act on the Protocol." So the fast-acting safety mechanism sits behind a slow-acting gate: someone has to write, review and pass a Spell before the circuit breaker can fire.

Standby Spells pre-pay that cost. A.1.10.5.2 describes them as a subset of Emergency Spells that let governance "bypass the GSM Pause Delay and directly perform crucial actions such as stopping an oracle, setting a debt ceiling to zero, disabling a D3M integration, or stopping liquidations for a collateral," and — critically — they or their factories "are reusable, meaning they can be executed several times if needed, or voted on again on a later date to be executed again."

The stated payoff is allocation of scarce attention: "In emergency scenarios, time is a scarce resource... Spell teams can then focus on crafting an ad hoc Emergency Spell to solve the root cause of an issue." Without Standby Spells, the first hours of an incident are spent building plumbing whose only job is to reach a switch that already exists.

A.1.10.5.2.1 also names the cost outright: "Standby Spells open new attack vectors that must be mitigated," delegating that mitigation to the Aligned Delegates' role in Standby Spells. A pre-approved, reusable, delay-bypassing action is by construction a standing loaded weapon — the same property that makes it fast in an emergency makes it valuable to an attacker who can get it fired.
description: MOM circuit breakers must be triggered by a Spell first; pre-authorized reusable Standby Spells remove that step from the critical path, at the cost of new attack surface.
